newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-FRENCH DIVA PIERCE STEPS INTO SPOTLIGHT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FRENCH DIVA PIERCE STEPS INTO SPOTLIGHT.

text.p: French tennis diva Mary Pierce plans to put her career back on centre stage in the Australian Open semifinals on Thursday, although the day may well belong to a new star, Swiss teenager Martina Hingis.
Pierce, making a grand comeback to Melbourne Park's Centre Court after winning here in 1995, faces 12th seed Amanda Coetzer for a place in her third grand slam final.
Pierce's expressive style has made her a favourite with the crowds and she will be counting on her fans to lift her against an in-form Coetzer.
South African Coetzer has got the bit between her teeth after ousting world number one Steffi Graf in the fourth round.
But their match is likely to take second billing to Thursday's other women's semifinal, between American Mary Joe Fernandez and Hingis, a 16-year-old poised to upstage them all.
The men's semifinals begin with an intriguing clash between world number two Michael Chang, a battle-wise veteran at the age of 24, and rising Spanish star Carlos Moya.
Hingis, the fourth seed, is the highest-ranked player left in the women's draw and is only two matches away from becoming the game's youngest grand slam champion for more than a century.
Hingis' playfulness on court is sometimes mistaken for teasing by the other players, but the prodigy is no child when it comes to weighing up her opposition.

"There's still so many good players around, especially in the semifinals. I don't think that just anybody can win a grand slam. It always must be a champion," she told reporters after beating Romania's Irina Spirlea in straight sets on Wednesday.
After only two years as a professional, Hingis has shown the hallmarks of a champion, refusing to yield a single set on her way to the semifinals.
She made light work of Fernandez less than two weeks ago in the semifinal of the Sydney International, but the American, a veteran of two finals in Melbourne, has experience on her side.
Pierce has regained her confidence in this tournament and showed a mental toughness some commentators say had been lacking in seeing off Belgian Sabine Appelmans on Tuesday.
Pierce was down 0-3 in the third set before she rallied to take the match.
Coetzer, a semifinalist here last year, is unlikely to let such a lead go. She didn't against Graf and is now third favourite behind Hingis and Pierce to lift the cup.
"The first grand slam of the year, you always see a few surprises I think," she said after demolishing unseeded American Kimberly Po in straight sets on Tuesday.

In the first men's semifinal, 20-year-old Moya will face a real test of class against Chang. Moya beat defending champion Boris Becker in the first round and has claimed some notable scalps since then.
He has already achieved Spain's best Australian Open result since Andres Gimeno lost to Rod Laver in the 1969 final. Nevertheless, few expect him to get past number two seed Chang.
